steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Is there really no possibility, director?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You know as well as I do that the remains of the Infected cannot be taken out for a funeral.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: What about the ashes?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Even the ashes must be processed to ensure that there is no risk prior to being removed.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: We've only recently established this office. The relevant facilities are not yet up to scratch.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: How long will it take?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Even if I submitted an application now, it would take at least six months for it to be approved by the landship and for the equipment to arrive.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: ...Do you realize how cruel this is?

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I was both her doctor and her only friend, but I couldn't even be by her side in her final moments.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Then, her remains were quarantined.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: And now I need to submit an application just to get her ashes back?

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: And this will take months?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Please, don't make this difficult.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You know why we have these rules. We wrote some of them together.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I've been working with Rhodes Island for a year now. I'm only asking for this one thing.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I couldn't travel with her when she was alive. The least I can do is take her ashes on a journey, now that she's gone.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: It was her final wish.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: We're doctors, Hourglass. We have a responsibility to others.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Are we supposed to act like emotionless robots just because we're doctors?!

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I don't want to argue with you about this, Hourglass.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I understand that you're grieving. I—

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: If the day comes when this happens to Schwarz...

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Would you still be trying to convince yourself with the same rules?!

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You—!

steps.name: Communications Terminal Announcement
steps.text: Disposition is about to begin.

steps.name: Communications Terminal Announcement
steps.text: Please enter your identification code, then enter the cremation chamber to begin the process.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Normally, all dispositions are handled by the office director, meaning me.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: If you want, I can let you handle this. Just this once.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: ...But I'm afraid that's all I can do.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I never got to say goodbye in her last moments. Now I'll never fulfill her final wish. How could I face her now?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: ...I see.
Dressed in full protective equipment, Ceylon deftly pushes the cart carrying Delia's body towards the cremator.
She has gotten used to seeing and dealing with the bodies of the Infected.
But this does not make it hurt any less.

a.text: 'If the day comes when this happens to Schwarz...'
'Would you still be trying to convince yourself with the same rules?!'

steps.text: There was clear anger in Hourglass's voice, but Ceylon willingly accepts it.
It is her duty to bear the brunt of such anger. She was prepared for it, ever since she decided to help Rhodes Island establish this office.
As for the question itself—
'It's none of your business what happens between me and Schwarz!'
She almost retorted with that, but of course she could not.
Just as she could not tell Hourglass that 'I understand your pain.'
Regardless of what made Hourglass say it, though, Ceylon had already lost count of how many nights she had spent crying over the possibility.
Every time, she wiped her tears dry, to continue to read the research and write the reports.
It is one of her firm beliefs that tears are less useful than medical research.
If the day comes when it is Schwarz lying on that cart, and it is somebody else pushing it, it could only be because she was prevented from finding a way to save her first.
In which case, she would accept it, she thinks.
She would have done everything she could, she thinks.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I'm sorry, Delia.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Things rarely go the way we want them to.
She pushes the body into the cremator.
After a moment of silence, she presses the button.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: ...Good night.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: What are you looking at?

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: The sea.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: She didn't like the sea. She said she'd gotten sick of it, after seeing it all her life.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: She always said she wanted to go on a journey. That she'd go once she'd saved up enough money. But it wasn't meant to be.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I've calmed down now. I'm sorry for shouting like that.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: It's alright. I'm glad you understand.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I'll hold a funeral for her in a few days.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Have you already made the arrangements?

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Yes. I started planning it long ago.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: The ashes were never necessary. I just wanted to give it one last try.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: You have nothing to apologize for. I know you're hurting too.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: But it's hard to keep your cool at a time like this.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Will you come to her funeral?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Of course.
A few days later
The road from Fashion Street to the shore is paved with flowers. Massive flower baskets line the sidewalks.
A temporary stage has been erected at the end of the street, with a dozen chairs set up in front of it.
A photo of Delia hangs high above the stage.

steps.name: Funeral Officiant
steps.text: Delia's parents died when she was young. She led a secluded life after contracting Oripathy, but she had a friend who stayed by her side until the very end—Renata.

steps.name: Funeral Officiant
steps.text: We'd like to invite Renata to come on stage.

steps.name: Funeral Officiant
steps.text: ...Excuse me, I have just been informed that Renata is unable to come, but she has prepared an audio recording for us to play.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Hourglass's Voice
steps.text: The first time I saw Delia, she was dancing by the seaside. Back then, I hated my life. I hated everything, and was even thinking of letting the sea take me.

steps.name: Hourglass's Voice
steps.text: But somehow, she seemed to know what was going through my head, and started dancing in front of me.

steps.name: Hourglass's Voice
steps.text: I will always remember that dance. The way she whirled and leapt across the beach, the way the hem of her dress shone in the sunlight.

steps.name: Hourglass's Voice
steps.text: These last few days, all I could think of was that dance, the one burned into my memories.

steps.name: Hourglass's Voice
steps.text: I compiled all my memories of her in an album. I thought that was enough.

steps.name: Hourglass's Voice
steps.text: I thought I was prepared for the day she would leave us.

steps.name: Hourglass's Voice
steps.text: But when I woke up from my dreams with a start, only to find once again that she was no longer there, I just couldn't do it anymore.

steps.name: Hourglass's Voice
steps.text: I miss her so much...
Ceylon feels overwhelmed by emotion. She cannot imagine how she would take it, if the day ever came when it was her turn to experience all this.
Schwarz still has time. Intellectually, she knows that she cannot truly understand what Hourglass is feeling right now.

Yet the fears conjured by her overactive imagination across all those tearful nights begin to overlap with the portrait of pain being painted by Hourglass, prying open the already-fragile barriers of her heart.
She wants to see Hourglass. She wants to talk to her.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Excuse me, sir, do you know where Hourglass... where Renata is?

steps.name: Funeral Officiant
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Is something the matter?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I'm her supervisor at work. You can trust me.

steps.name: Funeral Officiant
steps.text: ...She just gave me the recording and left. I don't know where she went.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I'm here, Delia.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: In the end, I lied to the director.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: She's sharp—it won't fool her for long.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: But I don't need much time for this.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: It won't take long for me to take you with me, for us to leave this place together, to go far, far away.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I'll take you to all the places we visited together.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: And all the places you wanted to go, but never could.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Then, we'll live quietly together, somewhere we can see the sunset.
Hourglass mutters as she searches for Delia's name on the shelf holding the ashes.
She has worked here as a doctor for over a year, and treated many patients. Her hand begins to tremble as she sees familiar name after familiar name.
Finally, she finds Delia's name.
The shelf is a little high. She finds a chair and drags it over. The screeching sound it makes on the floor echoes through the room, making her heart skip a beat.
She steps on the chair. With a trembling hand, she tries to put in the key to open the cabinet with Delia's name on it.
Perhaps her tears have clouded her vision, or perhaps her hand is trembling too much, but she cannot get it in.
She tries once, twice, many times.
Until the tears are all over her face.
Until the key slips from her hand.
Until she falls from the chair after bending down to pick up the key.
Until she is sitting on the ground in a daze.
Until she cannot hold it back anymore, and begins to cry her heart out.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I'm sorry, Delia.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: It's me. Is Hourglass there?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Director! I thought you asked her to come pick up Delia's ashes?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Where is she?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: She just left. Crying.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I need you to—

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Hm, that's odd.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Yes? What is it?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Something was obviously off about her, so I went in to see what was going on.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: She didn't take Delia's ashes?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: In fact, it looks like she didn't even open the cabinet.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: ...I'm coming back right now.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: How did she do it?

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: The way she taught me... first a spin, then another—

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Ouch!

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Look how clumsy I am. I could never dance with the passion that you did.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Hourglass!

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: How did you find me, director?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You mentioned the beach where you first met her, in your recording.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I immediately knew you must have meant this place. I used to play here all the time.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I stole your pass while you were at the funeral.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: That doesn't matter... Well, maybe it does a little. But why?

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: How do we prepare ourselves for the passing of a loved one?

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: You've always said you would do everything you can to prevent it.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: As for me, I recorded everything about her.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: And look what happened.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I haven't had a single night's sleep since she died.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I even broke the rules to steal her ashes.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Why didn't you then?

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: When I saw the shelf holding her ashes, I realized how meaningless it all was.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: It's not her ashes I wanted to take.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: She's dead.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: All I wanted was to see her one last time. And it made me do something so stupid.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: What finally hit me was that—

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: She's never coming back.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I wasn't ready for that.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: How could I be?
Ceylon sits down next to Hourglass.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: My father was always busy when I was little. Schwarz was both my bodyguard and my companion.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I liked to sneak out and walk towards the volcano.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I never managed to reach it, though, because Schwarz always stopped me partway.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: But there was always something fun, something interesting, at wherever she stopped me.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: And so I would enjoy myself there, and follow her home.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I always thought those days would last forever.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Until I learned what Oripathy was.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: And so I set my mind to curing her.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: To be honest, I'm even more selfish than you.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: If there's a chance I can cure her, I will seize it, even if it means sacrificing the time I get to spend with her.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I always thought that, this way, I could console myself when the time comes—that I gave her all the time I could.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: But it's just as you said. We were both wrong. All our preparations will mean nothing when our loved ones really leave us.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: It was hard enough listening to your recording at the funeral.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: If the day really does come when Schwarz leaves me... I would probably take it even worse than you did.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: That's how I used to be...

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: We're all the same, until we truly come face-to-face with the final farewell of death.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Proud, blind. Thinking we can take it.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: But when someone we love dies, they take part of us with them.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: We can never be whole again.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: If... just hypothetically...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: If you really did take her ashes... where would you go?

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I... I would have traveled with them.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I wanted to take her to all the places we've visited together.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I wanted to take her ashes to all the places we weren't able to.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: But... that's just wishful thinking.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: ...Go. Do it.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I said go do it.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I never told anyone that you stole my pass. Officially, you still have my permission to take Delia's ashes.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I'll go back to the landship and submit a formal application for you to go on your journey.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: There will a penalty, of course. I'm going to dock your pay for six months.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: We also don't have a suitable container in New Siesta yet. While I'm there, I'll ask Engineering to prepare one.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: That'll be quicker than waiting for them to send us one.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Wherever you go, however, you must report to the local Rhodes Island office and have your container examined.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: If anything dangerous happens, or if I find you spread her ashes anywhere—

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You're finished.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Other than that, though, I'll ask them to work with you and allow you to go wherever you want with Delia.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: ...But there's no point.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I know I said we were wrong. But were we?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: We raged against the dying of the light. If parting is inevitable, if we can never be whole again—

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Then, at the very least, the traces our loved ones left behind might fill in that hole, little by little.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I'm sorry for acting like I understand what you're going through.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Our situations are different. It's also not my place to order you to do anything. I just thought that, if the day ever comes for me...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I would go everywhere we had left our marks together and cry there. Just like you did.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Once I'd cried my heart out and my tears run dry, then I'd start thinking about what to do next.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: But if not even that works...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Then let's get together and talk again.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: ...Mm-hm.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: Thank you, director.

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: I'm not sure I can be as strong as all that...

steps.name: Hourglass
steps.text: But I'll try.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: How's my condition, Medic?

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: A little worse than last year.

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: You've been pushing yourself too hard these past couple years, both as an instructor and as an operator.

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: I'll put in a request to reduce your workload.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: But my reassignment request—

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: Would you stop pushing yourself once you get back to New Siesta?

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: I'll get plenty of rest.

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: Oh, please. You've been with us for two years now, you think we don't know you?

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: You'd never take care of yourself, not without someone forcing you to.

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: Ceylon would've been the best for the job, but with the New Siesta office just getting up and running, it's going to be at least a year before we're comfortable with letting you go back.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Then I'll care for her here on the landship.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: Lady Ceylon?!

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: Hey Ceylon. You're back already?

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: I was hoping to give Schwarz a little surprise, though.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Oh, did I interrupt you? Apologies.

steps.name: Ceylon, Outside the Door
steps.text: Okay, take 2!

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: Ahem. Anyway, there's no need to worry, Schwarz. We've come up with the perfect solution for your situation.

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: Which is—

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Ta-da!

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: And there you go. Soon after you returned, Ceylon made a request to stay on the landship for a while.

steps.name: Medic
steps.text: Anyway, problem solved. Now I'll give you two some space to catch up.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: Lady Ceylon... I thought you were busy in New Siesta.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I talked to Father. He agreed to give the green light for Rhodes Island on certain matters.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: They'll be fine without me for a while.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: I was doing fine by myself. You didn't need to worry.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Are you sure you weren't thinking about how to hide your condition from me?

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: Well... no. You would find out anyway.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: That's more like it.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Medic was right. You need rest.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: So let's go on a trip, Schwarz.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: Where to?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You know, I just remembered that you once told me about the city where you were born.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I've never been there.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: There's not much left of it.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Then we can leave something behind.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Besides, I know all about your time as mercenary, but you've never told me about your childhood.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: ...Why, all of a sudden?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I was just thinking... You watched me grow up. You know everything there is to know about me.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: But there's still so much about you I don't know. That's not fair, is it?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I'm nothing if not greedy, Schwarz.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Good. Then let's review your health report, and then we can start planning our trip.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: As you wish.
